question: A patient suffers damage to the orbit in a road traffic incident resulting in damage to the third cranial nerve. Which of the following signs will be present?
model_reasoning: Damage to the third cranial nerve (oculomotor nerve) affects both motor and parasympathetic functions. The parasympathetic fibers carried by the third cranial nerve innervate the sphincter pupillae muscle, which is responsible for pupillary constriction. Damage to these fibers will result in loss of pupillary constriction, leading to pupillary dilatation (mydriasis) due to the unopposed action of the sympathetic nervous system. The motor fibers of the third cranial nerve innervate most extraocular muscles, including the medial rectus. Damage to the medial rectus innervation means the eye cannot adduct (move medially). The lateral rectus muscle (innervated by the abducens nerve, CN VI) will be unopposed, causing the eye to deviate laterally, resulting in a lateral strabismus (exotropia). Therefore, the combination of pupillary dilatation and a lateral strabismus is characteristic of third cranial nerve damage.

Therefore, you would expect the tissue to be red below the mucogingival junction and light pink above it.
